memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When a man is cleansed from his discharge, he is to count off seven days for his ceremonial cleansing; he must wash his clothes and bathe himself with fresh water, and he will be clean.'" - Lev 15:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When the discharge stopped, the man did not simply walk back into normal life. He counted off seven days.

Picture him marking each one. Day two. Day four. Day six. Every day, closer to the water and the washing and the word clean.

There is something valuable in a countdown that runs towards freedom rather than away from it. Most of us are better at counting the days we have suffered than the days until restoration. We tally the losses. We keep score of how long it has been hard.

But this man's counting pointed forward. Each morning was one day nearer to being back at the tabernacle, back at the table, back among his people.

Scripture teaches us to count this way. Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom (Ps 90:12). And Paul, who suffered as much as anyone, wrote of light and momentary troubles achieving an eternal glory that far outweighs them all (2 Cor 4:17).

Whatever season you are in, it has a number of days, and God knows the number. You are not counting endlessly. You are counting towards something.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you count your hard days, or the days until restoration?
2. What are you actually moving towards right now?
3. How does an eternal perspective change today's difficulty?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me to number my days rightly. Turn my eyes from counting losses to counting Your faithfulness, and hold me steady until this season ends. Amen.
